clue.text: Scottish town in distress, easily torn apart

indicators.note: the town is placed in the middle of the word for distress

parts.note: distress means pain
Perth is a city on the Tay in Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish town in such distress that it is being easily torn apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flimsy enough to be easily torn has the thickness of a sheet of paper.

clue.text: More than one tool snaps, audibly

indicators.note: audibly means the word for snaps is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: snaps are photographs, informally pix

explanation.surface: Several tools break with an audible crack.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a pointed digging implement, so several tools rather than one.

clue.text: Business of PLC tied up with bus, train and harbour?

definitions.text: Business of PLC tied up with bus, train and harbour?

indicators.note: tied up suggests the letters are knotted together into a new order

parts.note: a harbour is a port

explanation.surface: A public limited company whose business is buses, trains and a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whole clue as a description of the answer as well as its wordplay: a company running such services is in this business.
explanation.definitionFit: Buses, trains and ferries are the services that make up a shared transit system.

clue.text: Article accepted by my Lord edited in an arbitrary way

indicators.note: the article is taken in by the other letters, so it goes inside them
edited means the words are reworked into a new order

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article taken in by a peer and then edited on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My Lord' is how a judge or peer is addressed; here it is just letters for 'edited' to rearrange, split by 'accepted by' after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without plan or pattern is acting at random, arbitrarily.

clue.text: Post unsuitable for someone who wants to be liked?

definitions.text: Post unsuitable for someone who wants to be liked?

parts.words: Post unsuitable for someone who wants to be liked?
parts.note: post here is letters received; someone hungry for popularity would not want correspondence full of loathing

explanation.surface: Advice that some mail is wrong for a people-pleaser.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive letters expressing loathing are the opposite of what a person craving approval wants.

clue.text: New astronomer initially taking in hazy blue gas cloud

indicators.note: the opening letters take in the jumbled word, enclosing it
initially points to the first letter of astronomer
hazy means the word blue is blurred into a new order

explanation.surface: A new astronomer spotting a hazy blue gas cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hazy blue' reads as the colour of the cloud, but 'hazy' is the anagram signal working on blue.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy, an interstellar cloud of dust and gas is called by this Latin word for mist.

clue.text: Shoemaker quiet about beginning to make it

indicators.note: the word for quiet goes about, surrounding, the other letters

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of make

explanation.surface: A cobbler being asked to keep quiet as he starts work.
explanation.walkthrough: A blacksmith or farrier makes horseshoes, so 'Shoemaker' is not a cobbler here.
explanation.definitionFit: A metalworker who forges and fits horseshoes makes shoes for horses.

clue.text: Second best game having the action interrupted

parts.note: best means top
Go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A second-rate game whose play keeps being stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: STOP-GO describes progress in fits and starts, as in British economic policy of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Something proceeding in fits and starts keeps halting and restarting.

clue.text: Imprisoned regularly, I'm free at last, but only just

parts.note: the nick is British slang for prison, so a prisoner is in it
oft is an old word for often, regularly
taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of free

explanation.surface: A prisoner celebrating release, but only by the narrowest margin.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving at the last possible moment means making it only just.

clue.text: One dishing out the basil, right?

definitions.text: One dishing out the basil, right?

indicators.note: dishing out suggests the letters are served up in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone handing out basil asks whether that is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishing out' rearranges THE BASIL R; the whole clue describes a seller of herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who grows or sells medicinal and culinary plants deals in herbs like basil.

clue.text: Conservative to help bringing in elected ministers

indicators.note: the word for helping brings in, encloses, the other piece

parts.note: to help is to abet
a party elected is in

explanation.surface: A Tory helping to bring elected ministers into office.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior ministers who form the government collectively make up this body.

clue.text: Fish line caught in hat

indicators.note: the letter is caught inside the hat word

parts.note: a boater is a flat straw hat

explanation.surface: A fishing line snagged in someone's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A herring cured by smoking is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Still gutted, I leave part of Ireland

indicators.note: gutted means the insides of still are removed, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Still devastated, someone departs from a part of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a county and town in the north-west of the Irish Republic.

clue.text: Spanish dance man dances round EU festival, getting called back

indicators.note: the jumbled man goes round, enclosing, the turned letters
dances means the letters of man move into a new order
called back means read backwards

parts.note: a gala is a festival

explanation.surface: A man dances around a European festival and is called back for an encore.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled man splits round the turned letters: M at the front, NA at the back. The answer is properly spelt with a tilde, malagueña.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fandango-like folk dance from Andalusia, notably Malaga.

clue.text: Call time possibly with the sound of a bell?

definitions.text: with the sound of a bell?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Calling time in a pub, perhaps with a ringing bell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CALL TIME; the bell rung at closing time sounds metallic.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringing, clanging tone like struck metal is what a bell gives.

clue.text: Moving car to appear in style — in one of these?

definitions.text: Moving car to appear in style — in one of these?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters appear in, inside, the word for style

parts.note: a mode is a style or fashion

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A car moving in style, as part of a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving car' looks like a definition by itself, but 'Moving' is the anagram signal, and the whole clue pictures the procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal procession of cars, as for a dignitary, is a stylish way to travel.

clue.text: Brief minutes one's taken

parts.note: min is the abbreviation for minutes
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A brief record of minutes in which one is noted as taken.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or adjective, this word means small or short, as in a skirt.

clue.text: Noble declines coming up to receive grant

indicators.note: the reversed word receives, encloses, the other piece
in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: declines means dips
to grant is to lend

explanation.surface: A nobleman whose fortunes are declining, rising again on receiving a grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses DIPS into SPID, which takes in LEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnificent or grand, as in a noble building, is a sense both words share.

clue.text: Empty threats securing a post

indicators.note: the word for empty threats secures, holds, the letter inside

parts.note: bluster is loud, empty threatening talk

explanation.surface: Idle threats made to secure a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pillar in a row supporting a rail is an upright post.

clue.text: Side with male, after a drink

indicators.note: the male letter comes after the drink

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Siding with a man after a drink together.
explanation.definitionFit: A side in sport is a squad of players.

clue.text: Fashionable logo carried by upper-class sweetheart

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: the logo word is carried inside the word for sweetheart

parts.note: pet is a term of endearment
a logo is a trademark, a mark

explanation.surface: A designer logo carried by a posh darling.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket goods are expensive and aimed at the fashionable, high-end customer.

clue.text: Important woman becoming a member of two unions?

definitions.text: becoming a member of two unions?

parts.note: important means big
Amy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An important woman joining two trade unions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unions' looks like trade unions, but it means marriages.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying while already married makes a person party to two marriages at once.

clue.text: Bet Queen accepts Welsh court worker

indicators.note: the two pieces accept the letter, taking it inside

parts.note: to lay a bet is to wager
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A gambler and a queen take in a Welshman working at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor or barrister is someone who works in the law courts.

clue.text: Exile to country's understood, after reversal in plot

indicators.note: the reversed word is put in the word for plot

parts.note: a ruse is a scheme or plot

indicators.note: the word for understood is read backwards

parts.note: tacit means understood without being said

explanation.surface: A plot to banish someone to the country, quietly understood after a reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: To rusticate is also, in British universities, to suspend a student and send them home for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin rus means countryside, so the verb means banish to rural parts.

clue.text: Force breaking into one may be inappropriate

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the word for one

parts.note: a unit is one
F is the symbol for force

explanation.surface: Breaking in by force may be an improper act.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not suited to a purpose is unsuitable or inappropriate.

clue.text: Name American river

parts.note: a tag is a name or label
US means American

explanation.surface: Naming an American river.
explanation.definitionFit: This river flows through Spain and Portugal to Lisbon.

clue.text: Abnormally shunning BR line? It turns up irregularly

indicators.note: shunning means leaving out the named letters

parts.note: taken as written: British Rail

explanation.surface: A railway line abnormally shunned by British Rail that rarely shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: Abnormally looks like the anagram signal but is the fodder: removing B, R and one L leaves the answer in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregularity or oddity is something that occurs out of the normal pattern.

clue.text: Making points time and time again during activity

indicators.note: the time letters fall during, inside, the activity word

parts.note: doing is activity

explanation.surface: Scoring points repeatedly during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking small spots or points on a surface.

clue.text: England's opening pair have a go at opening

parts.note: the first two letters of England
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: England's opening batting pair have a go at the start of play.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is a way in, an opening.

clue.text: Codicil left first third of estate to son, without one taking seat

parts.note: a rider is a clause added to a document
the first two of the six letters of estate

explanation.surface: A codicil leaving a third of the estate to a son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without one taking seat' describes a horse whose rider is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking anyone in the saddle means having no rider aboard.
